principles: Gate messages must carry the copy-pastable remedy, not just the diagnosis
Provenance evidence must be durable and per-session attributable before it can be enforced
Never silently break the documented legitimate reviewer flow (Claude subagent reviewers share the owner session per EXP-001)
Rollout follows shadow/warn/enforce; honesty about coordination-level (non-cryptographic) identity limits
drivers: B-f458: 14h/89-advance stall for want of a one-line hint
B-8038 root cause + B-3928 19-56s self-signs: reviewer-labeled passes with no writer identity
Codex multi-thread sessions are mechanically distinguishable (distinct ppid-derived ids); same-host subagents are not

options.name: A-record-only
cons: Self-sign still silently succeeds; user asked for validation, not just recording

options.name: B-record-plus-warn-default-enforce-optin
pros: Persists writerSessionId/sessionSource in signature domain (durable attribution)
Same-session writes get a visible persisted flag + stderr warning; enforce config rejects them where hosts have real session separation (Codex multi-thread)
Does not break Claude subagent flow by default
cons: On Claude host the flag cannot distinguish subagent from owner self-sign (EXP-001) so warn text must be carefully neutral
Signature domain change needs versioned verification for legacy records

options.name: C-dispatch-token-binding
pros: Strongest mechanical wedge: pass must reference an owner-minted dispatch record; latency dispatch-to-pass becomes auditable
cons: Bigger build touching dispatch/review_run/pass lifecycle; overlaps existing channel-gate dispatch evidence; scope creep for this story

rationale: Option B delivers exactly what the user asked (record writer session; validate vs owner lease session) at the strongest level that does not reject the documented legitimate Claude reviewer flow. Warn-default with persisted selfSignSuspect flag makes B-3928/B-f458-style self-signs visible in the operator output and in durable records; enforce stays available as config for hosts with genuine per-thread session separation. Option C is noted as the natural layer-3 follow-up.

preMortem.scenario: Enforce accidentally becomes default and every Claude-host reviewer pass is rejected
preMortem.trigger: Config default set to enforce or warn/enforce flag inverted
preMortem.mitigation: Default warn hardcoded in resolver fallback; contract test asserts default mode is warn and that a same-session pass in warn mode still persists

preMortem.scenario: New signature domain breaks verification of legacy passes
preMortem.trigger: signReviewPass recomputation includes writerSessionId for records that never had it
preMortem.consequence: canPassReviewGuard fail-closed on all existing stories mid-flight
preMortem.mitigation: Versioned signing: records without writerSessionId verify via legacy domain; new records include it; regression test with a legacy fixture

preMortem.scenario: Warn flag floods every legitimate Claude pass making the signal worthless noise
preMortem.trigger: Flag text reads as accusation and gates/tools start consuming it as blocking
preMortem.consequence: Operators ignore all provenance warnings; alert fatigue
preMortem.mitigation: Neutral flag semantics (same_session_write: subagent-or-self, mechanically indistinguishable per EXP-001) + this story does NOT wire the flag into any blocking gate; gate consumption is explicitly out of scope

preMortem.scenario: Session id spoofing via explicit-env override lets a self-sign masquerade as a distinct session
preMortem.trigger: Owner exports a fabricated session env before calling review_pass_set
preMortem.mitigation: Persist sessionSource alongside id (explicit-env vs derived-ppid vs host-adapter); document that explicit-env writers are coordination-level claims; forgery remains detectable in audit via source field and lease history
